children: SpaceX is expanding its push into mobile connectivity through an agreement to acquire nationwide 800 MHz wireless spectrum from Grain Management.

The deal could help Elon Musk's company extend Starlink Mobile coverage beyond areas typically served by satellite connectivity. The transaction requires Federal Communications Commission approval, and financial terms have not been disclosed.

Low-band spectrum can travel longer distances and penetrate buildings more effectively than higher-frequency bands, potentially helping SpaceX address coverage challenges as it develops its satellite-based cellular service. Most existing phones support the 800 MHz band, although compatibility with the planned service remains uncertain.

The agreement weighed on shares of established wireless carriers. AT&T (T) fell 6% to $23.25 in after-hours trading Thursday, while Verizon (VZ) dropped 5.85% to $43.64 and T-Mobile US (TMUS) declined 6.63% SpaceX
shares fell 4.19% during Thursday's session before gaining 2.32% in late trading.
The acquisition could expand SpaceX's competitive reach in wireless communications, though regulatory approval and execution remain key hurdles before the planned service can scale.

title: AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile Stocks Sink as SpaceX Expands Cellular Ambitions
